previews.heading: Model Previews
previews.subtitle: Control background preview generation for the whole instance.
previews.infoScope: This only affects the small 3D thumbnail shown on model cards (Models, Collections) — never the full model viewer. It also only applies to files with no thumbnail yet: an embedded thumbnail from a sliced .3mf file, or one already generated before, is always reused automatically regardless of this setting. This choice only decides what happens for the rest — typically .stl/.obj files, or a .3mf with no embedded thumbnail:
previews.infoAutomatic: Automatic — a visitor's browser renders and saves the missing thumbnail as soon as its card scrolls into view.
previews.infoOnDemand: On demand — a card shows a "Generate preview" button instead; nothing renders until someone clicks it.
previews.infoDisabled: Disabled — cards always show a placeholder; a thumbnail is never rendered.
previews.automaticDesc: Load missing previews only as cards enter view, then save them for future visits.
previews.onDemandDesc: Show saved previews immediately and generate missing ones only when requested.
previews.disabledDesc: Never generate card previews. Interactive viewing remains available by opening a model.

triggers.deleteAllTitle: Delete all models for a user
triggers.deleteAllDesc: Permanently deletes every model a user created, uploaded, or imported — files included. Their categories and collections are left in place, just empty.
triggers.deleteFailed: Failed to delete this user's models.

thingiverse.helpText: Create an app at thingiverse.com/apps/create (any type, e.g. "Desktop") and paste the Access Token it shows you.
thingiverse.statusConfigured: An Access Token is currently configured.
thingiverse.statusNotConfigured: No Access Token is configured yet -- Thingiverse imports will fail until one is set.
thingiverse.tokenPlaceholder: Paste a new token to replace the current one
thingiverse.tokenHelperConfigured: For security, the current token is never shown again -- leave this blank to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it.

session.heading: Session Length
session.subtitle: Control how long a signed-in session stays valid for the whole instance.
session.infoBody: How long a freshly issued sign-in token stays valid before that user is asked to log in again. Applies instance-wide to every new login, registration, and email verification. Changing this only affects tokens issued from now on -- anyone already signed in keeps whatever length was active when they logged in.
session.invalid: Enter a number between 300 (5 minutes) and 31536000 (1 year) seconds.

smtp.helpText: Used to send the account-verification email on registration. Leave Host blank to turn email verification off entirely — new accounts are then verified and signed in immediately.
smtp.statusConfigured: SMTP is configured — new accounts must verify their email before signing in.
smtp.statusNotConfigured: SMTP is not configured — new accounts are verified and signed in immediately.
smtp.secureHint: Enable for port 465. Leave off for STARTTLS on port 587.
smtp.passwordPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the current password

database.helpText: Host and port always reflect the DATABASE_URL this instance was started with and can't be changed here. Database, user, and password can be switched live — the new credentials are tested before anything is applied, so a typo can't take the app down, but the switch only affects this running process and won't survive a restart.
database.passwordPlaceholder: Required to test and apply a switch
database.confirmWarning: This repoints every database call this running instance makes at a different database. If the new credentials are wrong or unreachable, the switch is rejected and nothing changes.

extension.heading: Thingport Grab
extension.intro: A browser extension that imports MakerWorld, Thingiverse, and Printables models straight from their own pages.
extension.name: Thingport Grab

chrome.heading: Install Thingport Grab
chrome.step1: Unzip the downloaded file somewhere permanent -- Chrome loads the extension from this folder every time it starts.
chrome.step2: Open chrome://extensions in a new tab.
chrome.step4: Click "Load unpacked" and select the unzipped folder.
chrome.step5: Click the new Thingport icon in your toolbar and enter your instance URL and login.

firefox.heading: Install Thingport Grab
firefox.step1: Open the downloaded .xpi file directly, or drag it onto a Firefox window.
firefox.step2: Click "Add" on Firefox's install confirmation prompt.
firefox.step3: Click the new Thingport icon in your toolbar and enter your instance URL and login.

bridge.heading: Thingport Bridge
bridge.intro: A small helper app that runs on your computer so "Open in Slicer" can hand a model straight to your slicer.

modal.startedNote: Your download should start automatically. Follow these steps to finish installing:

windows.heading: Install on Windows
windows.step1: Double-click the downloaded .exe (or run it with no arguments from a terminal). It installs itself and registers the protocol automatically.

linux.heading: Install on Linux
linux.step1: If your file manager blocks execution, mark the file as executable first.
linux.step2: Then run it once -- double-click, or from a terminal.

macos.heading: Install on macOS
macos.step2: Remove the Gatekeeper quarantine flag -- downloaded files are quarantined automatically.
macos.step3: Install it. This copies the app into ~/Applications and registers the thingport:// link.
macos.note: If macOS still refuses to run it, open System Settings -> Privacy & Security and allow it there instead.
